evidence.reviewer_disagreement_reviewed: The skeptic asked why this was not caught by PR #84's green run, since an hreflang-reciprocity test already existed and passed. Answered rather than deflected: that test asserts the languageAlternates MAP and the rendered SITEMAP, both of which were genuinely reciprocal. The divergence was in buildSpanishNicheMetadata, which hardcoded its languages and never read the map, so page metadata was one-way while both validated artifacts looked correct. The lesson recorded in the code comment is that validating a data source is not validating the output, and the new tests assert the emitted metadata directly.
evidence.winner_rationale: Reading the shared map is strictly better than a per-slug hardcode: it removes a special case, makes every pair live in one place, and means the English and Spanish sides cannot drift again. Fallback to self-reference preserves correct behaviour for pages that genuinely have no counterpart.

The single suite failure is pre-existing and unrelated (see tests_or_validation object).
